newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares defied all predictions of a limited rally to surge forward on Monday, sparked by a surprise rally on Wall Street.

Robust U.S. jobs growth in December had spread initial fears that the Dow would drop on Friday and South African shares had shed value. But the Dow stunned observers to close at a fourth record high, leaving the South African market seen as oversold.
As soon as trade kicked off on Monday buyers poured into stocks and prices rose across the board.
"It has been a really strong day," one dealer said.

Market observers had initially predicted early gains would not hold as futures-sellers would come into the market to sell equities at the higher prices, but after a slight dip early on stock prices rarely looked back.
A predicted late rash of profit-taking also failed to materialise and the main indices closed near day highs.

The all-share index rose 84 points to 6,758.6 as industrials added 91.4 points to 8,130.7. A lot of buying came in the form of baskets of major blue-chips, with demand coming from local institutions and overseas investors.
Corporate finance deals and assets swaps were also a feature of the day, especially in fuels group Sasol and First National Bank, dealers said.
"A lot of the trade took the form of corporate finance deals," one dealer said. Volumes were healthy with more than 600 million rands worth of shares changing hands.
Most blue-chips rose as De Beers ended up 375 cents to 134 rand, Richemont finished up one rand to 65.50 rand and SA Breweries added 175 cents to 123.50 rand.

There were few individual features on the day but information technology group Persetel lost 155 cents to end at 37.50 rand after announcing a German buy on profit-taking and market worries over the deal's price-tag.
Dealers said that all eyes would be on Wall Street's performance overnight to see if the day's rally could be sustained. Most were pessimistic, saying such heady gains had now over-inflated prices.
"Any fall on Wall Street tonight and all this will come down like a house of cards," one dealer said.

The battered gold sector had a more buoyant day as the price of bullion launched a tentative rally and news emerged that the Dutch central bank had managed to sell 300 tonnes of the yellow metal recently.
The news relieved dealers that the sickly market had absorbed so much gold, but may prove bearish in the long-term.
"Gold shares had a good day and made a pleasent change for everyone," one dealer said.
The gold index rose 38.4 points, or 2.7 percent, to 1,460.2. Vaal Reefs added 500 cents to 300 rand, Kloof was up 50 cents to 36.50 rand and Western Deeps was up 300 cents to 131.50 rand.
The share futures market also had a good day and made headway on its early Wall Street-inspired gains.

The value of the all-share March contract jumped to 6,315/25 from 6,185 as the industrials contract broke through the 8,000 mark to 8,012/23 from 7,875. The gold contract rallied to 1,032/40 from 1,007.
-- Paul Harris, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
